design: Graph-discriminating case. Everything works except one cross-corpus restriction with a weak textual pointer: A1-HIA 7's first limb excludes the Art 19(1)(a) consent derogation for genetic information, whatever the purpose. Art 19 itself does not mention Subregion law and Art 21(2) does not list 19(1)(a); the restriction is reached through Art 8(3) delegation, the citation graph's lower-level pointer, or the generated graph's restricts_route link. Misreading risk: only A1-HIA 7's second limb is limited to insurance and employment.

requirements.why: Art 6(1)(a) consent (clear written specific statement, Art 7(1)), and arguably 6(1)(b) under the terms of care.

Art 8(2)(c) health care on the basis of A1-HIA 4 (registered practitioners), as the clinic states; 8(2)(a) explicit consent is also available because A1-HIA 7's consent bar applies only to insurance or employment purposes.

The clinic relies on 19(1)(a), which A1-HIA 7 excludes for genetic information. No recognition covers the transfer (Annex II: certified recipients only, and not sensitive information); no approved clauses; 19(1)(b) needs a contract between the person and the custodian that the transfer is necessary to perform, and the terms of care do not cover referrals abroad; 19(1)(c) needs the person to be incapable of consent; 19(1)(d) has no public-interest basis. Cure: execute the approved clauses with an Art 18(2) assessment.
A1-HIA 7, first limb: genetic information may not be made the subject of an outward transfer on the basis of Art 19(1)(a). Not limited by purpose. The transfer as described relies on exactly that.
Disclosure by registered practitioners to a third party with the patient's consent (s.5(2)).
Not an outward transfer of patient records for hosting or storing them.
One person; not hosting a patient record system by an agent outside A1; no insurer matching.
Harrow bills no insurer and is not an insurer, so it is not a covered provider (B-HRA 2, 3(1)).
Harrow keeps the referral for its own care, not on behalf of another person: not a data host.

routes.why: A1-HIA 7 first limb. Occasional and informed consent are not enough.
Annex II: certified recipients only and not sensitive information; Harrow holds no certificate.
Executing the approved clauses with an Art 18(2) assessment would cover the transfer; Harrow is not a computing provider, so B-RAA production orders do not reach it.

must_not.why: Relying on Art 19(1)(a) for genetic information: the decisive trap.
Ruling out Art 8(2)(a) consent with A1-HIA 7's second limb, which applies only to insurance or employment purposes.
